SMTO-HTTP-0026 — The file couldn't be prepared for upload

GUID: f04bc4b9-03d6-4e64-9ffc-f4859be428d0
Slug: http-upload-invalid
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO tried to upload a file to a web service, but the Gateway (the helper program that sends SMTO's web requests) got file data it couldn't use, or files too large together. Nothing was uploaded.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the files for one upload add up to 8 MB or less. If they are larger, ask SMTO to upload them in separate requests. The Gateway refuses uploads over 8 MB in total.
  2. Add the file again with Add files to conversation in the message box, then ask SMTO to upload the new copy. A fresh copy replaces file data the Gateway couldn't read.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways. If the Gateway shows Update available, expand it and select its Update button once its running tasks are finished. A Gateway that doesn't match SMTO's version may not receive the file data SMTO sends.

What success looks like

  • SMTO uploads the file and shows the service's reply instead of this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend the same file unchanged over and over; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway could not build the HTTP upload because the private file envelope is missing, a referenced source is absent or has invalid base64 or metadata, or the files exceed 8 MiB in total.

What this means

  • The Gateway lacks a referenced private file envelope or its source has missing fields, invalid base64/metadata, unsafe delimiters or aggregate bytes beyond the upload bound. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The Gateway lacks a referenced private file envelope or its source has missing fields, invalid base64/metadata, unsafe delimiters or aggregate bytes beyond the upload bound.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the granted context references with their private envelope metadata and bounded sizes without publishing file contents.

How to fix it

  • gateway_core/http_files.prepare_upload raises this when a referenced context_id has no entry in the private_files envelope, base64 decoding fails, the source name or media type contains CR, LF or NUL, or the decoded total exceeds 8 MiB; gateway_core/http_client.py raises it when the private upload envelope is missing entirely. Re-grant the files to the conversation, keep the aggregate within 8 MiB, and confirm the Server and Gateway versions match if the envelope is absent.
  • Supply a valid authorized context-backed upload reference.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Each granted source validates and the complete supported upload remains within its limits.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
